subject: mathematics
question_text: If A = {0, π/6, π/4, π/3, π/2} and f: A→B is a surjection defined by f(x) = cos x then find B.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.79 — VSAQ chapter 14 Functions, question 90.2. The book prints NO internal mark split on its VSAQ pages (unlike its LAQ/SAQ pages): the 1+1 across the two steps is our division of the 2 marks, not the source's. Appearance years are the book's, board-split. Publisher's claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find B — the values you compute, and why B is exactly that set.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Compute every image
steps.margin_note: One mark for the five standard cosine values. These are table values — write them exactly, not as decimals.
steps.memory_tip: Five standard cosine values, written exactly as surds and fractions — not as decimals.

recall.must_convey: The five standard values: cos 0 = 1, cos π/6 = √3/2, cos π/4 = 1/√2, cos π/3 = 1/2, cos π/2 = 0.
accept: cos zero is one cos pi by six is root three by two cos pi by four is one by root two cos pi by three is half cos pi by two is zero
the standard cosine values one root three by two one by root two half and zero
substitute each angle into cosine and use the table values
cos values one root three by two one by root two half zero
evaluate cosine at each of the five angles

steps.why: The images are just the standard table, but they must be exact — a decimal is not the value the examiner wants.
common_mistakes: Swapping cos π/6 and cos π/3 — the two most confused values.
Writing decimals such as 0.866 instead of √3/2.

steps.label: Write B as a set
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the SET. Surjection means B is exactly the range; no value repeats here.
steps.memory_tip: Surjection means B IS the range, so B = f(A). Here no value repeats.
lines: f is a surjection ⇒ B = f(A)

recall.must_convey: That because f is a surjection, B is the set of those five values.
accept: since f is onto B is the range which is one root three by two one by root two half and zero
B is the set of the five cosine values
surjection means the codomain is exactly the range so B is that set
B equals one root three by two one by root two one half zero

steps.why: Every value is different here, so unlike the previous question nothing collapses — but the reason B equals the range is the same word: surjection.
common_mistakes: Writing B as an interval such as [0, 1] rather than the five-element set.
Omitting 0 or 1, the two endpoint values.

insider_note: Surjection is the whole clue: it means B equals the image set exactly, so B is just the five cosine values. All five are standard angles, so no decimal work is intended.
